name: Atlanta & the Dirty South
blurb: The trap's home base — where 808s got darker, hi-hats got faster, and the tempo of Southern rap changed permanently.

artists.name: Gucci Mane
artists.note: Early trap-era Atlanta voice; helped define the genre's lyrical and sonic template alongside producers like Zaytoven.

artists.name: Future
artists.note: Popularized the melodic, Auto-Tuned delivery over dark 808 production that came to define a huge swath of mainstream trap.

artists.name: Migos
artists.note: Known for triplet flow (three syllables per beat) that became one of the most widely imitated rhythmic patterns in all of rap nationally.

name: Memphis
blurb: Dark, horror-movie soul flipped into some of the eeriest, most influential low-end in rap — the direct ancestor of a lot of modern drill and trap.

artists.name: Three 6 Mafia
artists.note: The most influential group from the scene — DJ Paul and Juicy J's production defined the horrorcore-meets-rap aesthetic later cited by drill producers worldwide.

artists.name: Playa Fly
artists.note: Known for extremely fast chopped flows layered over the same dark, minimal Memphis instrumentals.

name: Bay Area (Oakland / Vallejo / SF)
blurb: Funk-bass-driven, uptempo, and unapologetically regional — hyphy and mob music built a scene almost entirely on its own terms.

artists.name: Mac Dre
artists.note: Considered the godfather of hyphy — his catalog basically defines the era's uptempo, bass-heavy party sound.

artists.name: E-40
artists.note: Longest-running architect of the Bay's slang-driven, bass-forward sound; also a key bridge between mob music and hyphy eras.

name: New York City
blurb: The birthplace — boom bap's sample-chopping, jazz/soul-sourced sound, and lyricism-first ethos still shapes what 'classic' hip-hop production means.

artists.name: Nas
artists.note: Illmatic is a foundational document of the sample-driven, jazz-inflected New York boom-bap sound of the early-to-mid 90s.

artists.name: Mobb Deep
artists.note: Defined a darker, grittier strain of the same boom-bap tradition — sparse piano/string loops over hard drums.

name: Detroit
blurb: Soul-sample chopping raised to an art form, plus its own rapid-fire, bounce-heavy street sound that's distinct from both coasts.

artists.name: J Dilla
artists.note: Producer whose sample-chopping and 'human' swung drum programming reshaped production far beyond Detroit — one of the most cited influences in hip-hop production generally.

artists.name: Danny Brown
artists.note: Blends Detroit's sample-based tradition with abrasive, genre-crossing modern production and a distinctly Detroit cadence.

name: Florida
blurb: From Miami bass's booming low end to modern Florida trap's especially chaotic, high-energy variant — a state with several distinct scenes.

artists.name: Uncle Luke / 2 Live Crew
artists.note: Foundational to Miami bass — booming 808s and electro-influenced uptempo production built specifically for sound systems and dancing.

artists.name: Kodak Black
artists.note: Pompano Beach — melodic but street-rooted delivery over that denser, harder South Florida trap production.
